findings.reason: Three explicit configuration names replace boolean pairs and exclude the invalid combination. All three selector/ignore choices match previously tested branches.

The three cases exercise the same checkpoint mapping, loaded weight parity and forward oracle. Keeping the shared loader/output test avoids duplicated fixtures and parity code. Explicit mode names make the distinct ignored-BF16 path clear.
Rename to online quantization preserves latent and shared outputs; routed-experts-only intentionally leaves these projections BF16. No assertions or numerical bounds change.

Adding Marlin to the shared unquantized-oracle fallback would alter default behavior across all models. The explicit optional factory override is restricted to supported Grug online FP8 ignored expert layers and preserves default rejection, the user-authorized narrow scope and the component control. Runtime math and global configuration stay unchanged.
